clue.text: Fruit that's scanned by electricity, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase before it is to be spoken, giving words that sound alike

parts.note: scanned is READ (said like the colour) and electricity is CURRENT

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit passed under some electrical scanner at the checkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to speak READ CURRENT; spoken, the past tense READ matches the colour word and CURRENT matches the dried-fruit word.
explanation.definitionFit: A small red berry from a garden bush, so it is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: More than one frill changes suit for one's benefit

definitions.meaning: pleated starched collars of Elizabethan dress
in bridge and whist, trumps a trick when out of the suit led

explanation.surface: Several frills alter a suit to flatter the wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing but is a card suit: to ruff is to play a trump when you cannot follow suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffs are frilled collars; to ruff is to trump, switching to the trump suit to win a trick.

clue.text: Article penned by artist on strike with a religious leader

indicators.note: penned by means the article sits inside the artist's name

parts.note: Salvador Dali, the Spanish surrealist painter
a is the indefinite article
to lam is to strike or thrash

explanation.surface: An article written by a striking artist alongside a spiritual leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on strike' suggests industrial action; 'on' just joins, and strike is LAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Naive journalist wrongly dropping a useful connexion

indicators.note: wrongly asks for a rearrangement, and dropping says one piece is left out of it

explanation.surface: A gullible reporter is mistaken to lose a helpful contact.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange NAIVE JOURNALIST after taking out one A; 'connexion' is the old spelling of connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A universal joint is a mechanical coupling letting shafts at an angle transmit rotation, a handy coupling.

clue.text: Echo in theatre, so undesirable

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie within the following words

explanation.surface: An echo in a theatre is so unwelcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To resound is to echo or ring with sound, the verb sense of echo.

clue.text: New clue confused American in centre

indicators.note: confused says the letters of clue are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fresh clue baffled an American at the heart of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central core of something, so its centre.

clue.text: Irish author initially identified with Great Britain

definitions.text: Irish author initially identified with Great Britain

parts.words: Irish author initially identified with Great Britain
parts.note: the Dublin-born playwright George Bernard, whose first two initials are GB, the abbreviation for Great Britain

explanation.surface: An Irish writer who came to be regarded as a British figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like 'at first', but it means 'by his initials': the playwright signed himself GBS.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was a Dublin-born playwright, so an Irish author whose initials begin GB.

clue.text: Is caught in the bungled robbery

indicators.note: caught in puts the first word inside the rearranged one
bungled means botched, so the letters of the are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is arrested in the botched robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungled' makes HET, and 'caught in' places the other word inside it; the surface reads as an arrest at a botched job.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, especially a large organised one.

clue.text: Affected by moving air, some musicians cried

parts.note: the winds are the wind players of an orchestra
cried means wept

explanation.surface: Some musicians wept, battered by the gale.
explanation.definitionFit: Windswept means exposed to or blown about by strong wind.

clue.text: They check wheels on their watch es that have stopped

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'They check wheels on their watch es that have stopped': the fragment 'es' is garbled, the scan does not show the down clues past 3, and a search for the text found nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: They check wheels on their watch es that have stopped

clue.text: Rash actions get one retreating in poor shape, surrounded by enemies

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the word before it inside the enemies word

parts.note: enemies are foes

indicators.note: retreating tells us the numeral one moves back to the end of its word

parts.note: being in poor shape is being ill
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Reckless deeds leave a soldier falling back, battered and hemmed in by the foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' moves the numeral to the back of its word, making LLI; 'surrounded by' then puts that inside the enemies.
explanation.definitionFit: Follies are foolish or reckless acts, so a fair synonym for rash actions.

clue.text: Food for crow? A rook tucked into corn I put out

indicators.note: tucked into puts the first pieces inside the anagrammed letters
put out means disturbed, so the letters of corn and I are rearranged

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A crow's dinner: a rook gets stuck into some corn that was put out for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' turns CORN + I into CRION; 'tucked into' sets A + R after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Crows feed on dead flesh, so rotting meat is food for crows; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Transparency shown by government that facilitates calculations

parts.note: a transparency is a photographic slide
government is rule

explanation.surface: A government showing transparency in a way that makes its sums easier to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide rule is a scaled instrument used before calculators to do multiplication and division.

clue.text: Lots of classical goddesses

definitions.meaning: lots are destinies, what falls to one in life
the three Greek goddesses who spin and cut the thread of life

explanation.surface: A great many deities from ancient Greece and Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots are fortunes or destinies, and the three Moirai were the classical goddesses of destiny.

clue.text: Singer bringing in right instrumental group

indicators.note: bringing in has the singer take another letter inside

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer

explanation.surface: A vocalist who draws in the right band of players.
explanation.definitionFit: The brass is the section of an orchestra or band playing trumpets, horns and trombones.

clue.text: From HQ, head of military and others providing lead, perhaps

parts.note: headquarters is a base

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of military

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: Coming from headquarters, the head of the army and the others take the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and others' is the full sense of ET AL; 'lead' is the metal, not leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is an example of a base metal, a common non-precious one; perhaps marks the example.

clue.text: Waste one's little drink? Girlfriend consumes it

indicators.note: consumes means the girlfriend word swallows the pieces before it

parts.note: a date is a girlfriend or partner one goes out with
one's is I (one) plus S
a sip is a little drink

explanation.surface: Wasting your small drink? Your girlfriend will happily drink it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumes' is the container signal: the girlfriend word is split around the little-drink pieces, while 'it' just refers back to the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissipate is to squander or fritter away, the verb sense of waste.

clue.text: Energy I'm getting in a group of people

indicators.note: getting in puts the first word inside the following ones

parts.note: a nation is a people
I'm without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: I feel energised when I join a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness and vigour, so energy.

clue.text: Less serious broadcaster securing venue for concert

indicators.note: securing means the broadcaster word holds the venue inside it

parts.note: a sower broadcasts, scattering seed
a concert hall is a venue

explanation.surface: A lighter-weight radio presenter who has booked a concert venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcaster' suggests radio but is a sower of seed, who broadcasts by scattering it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallower means having less depth, figuratively less serious or thoughtful.

clue.text: Aspiring to achieve first in Wimbledon, double-faulted

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of Wimbledon
faulted means gone wrong, so the letters of double are rearranged

explanation.surface: A player hoping to win at Wimbledon serves a double fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulted' makes OULDBE; the tennis picture of a double fault hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A would-be author is an aspiring one, someone hoping to become it.

clue.text: Visibly embarrassed over large amount in new version

parts.note: red-faced, blushing
a raft is a large number or quantity

explanation.surface: Blushing about a mass of material that needs rewriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A redraft is a draft written again, a revised version of a document.

clue.text: Card game in which you can make very little without spades

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the very-little word wraps the spades letter

parts.note: a whit is the smallest amount
S is the bridge abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card game where you score almost nothing if you hold no spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside': WHIT goes round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Whist is a classic trick-taking card game for four players.

clue.text: Like aggressive male scientist before getting old

parts.note: Ernst Mach was an Austrian physicist

explanation.surface: Describing a combative man, a scientist who arrived before he grew old.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes an aggressively masculine man, so an adjective like aggressive male.

clue.text: Very skilful attempt

definitions.meaning: a try, as in have a go

explanation.surface: A highly skilled try.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack shot is very skilful, and having a crack at something is an attempt.

clue.text: Less than four inches? It's deceptive

definitions.meaning: a hand is a measure of four inches, used for horses, so something below a hand

explanation.surface: Something measuring under four inches turns out to be misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: A hand, the unit for a horse's height, is four inches.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand means sly or done secretly, so deceptive; read literally it is under a hand's height.

clue.text: Beautiful young woman in otherwise boring commercial

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman features in an otherwise dull advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in otherwise' says this is another sense: a dryad, a wood nymph, by extension a beautiful young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph, and nymph is also used of a beautiful young woman.

clue.text: Prepared for race — ran along track

definitions.meaning: an athlete coached for a contest
went along railway lines, travelled by rail

explanation.surface: An athlete who got ready for a race by running round the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Trained means coached and prepared; it can also mean travelled by train along a railway track.

clue.text: Pleasantness of French in entering into friendly relations

indicators.note: entering has the French word go into the friendship word

parts.note: amity is friendship, friendly relations
en is French for in

explanation.surface: The charm of the French as they enter into friendly dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a pleasant quality or feature of a place, an old sense of pleasantness.

clue.text: So-called physician who wrote one or two books

definitions.meaning: Paul calls this evangelist the beloved physician

definitions.text: who wrote one or two books
definitions.meaning: the author of a Gospel and, traditionally, the Acts of the Apostles

explanation.surface: A doctor in name only who has written a book or two.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Luke is called a physician in Colossians and is credited with the third Gospel and Acts.

clue.text: Flew without one boy that's thrown out of plane

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the flying word goes around the others

parts.note: to jet is to fly, so flew is jetted
one is the Roman numeral I
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A plane flew on without a boy, who had been thrown out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking': the flying word goes round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw cargo out of an aircraft or ship.
